test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A wire encloses an area of 18634 cm², when it is bent in the form of a circle. The same wire is now bent to form a rectangle whose sides are in the ratio 5 : 6. The length (in cm) of the shorter side of the rectangle is (Take π = frac{{22}}{7}):
solution:
**Given:**

Area of the formed circle = 18634 cm²

Ratio of sides of the rectangle = 5 : 6

**Formula used:**

Area of a circle = πr²

Perimeter of a circle = 2πr

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2(l + b)

Here, r = radius of the circle,

l = length of the rectangle,

And, b = breadth of the rectangle

**Calculation:**

Let the radius of the formed circle be r

Now, πr² = 18634

⇒ r² = 18634 × frac{{7}}{22}

⇒ r² = 5929

⇒ r = 77

So, radius = 77 cm

Here perimeter of the formed circle will be equal perimeter of the rectangle

Let the sides of the rectangle be 5x and 6x

So, 2 × frac{{22}}{7} × 77 = 2(5x + 6x)

⇒ 2 × 22 × 11 = 2 × 11x

⇒ x = 22

Sides of the rectangle = 5 × 22 = 110 cm and 6 × 22 = 132 cm

So, the smallest side of the rectangle = 110 cm

**∴ The length (in cm) of the shorter side of the rectangle is 110.**
